To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of dental auxiliaries to examine schoolchildren for dental caries is feasible, and that the use of auxiliaries in this way is associated with a small reduction in the prevalence of caries compared with the use of dentists.

(a) the use of trained dental auxiliaries to examine children in dental epidemiologic surveys is feasible and reliable, (b) the use of clinical dental assistants to collect data on children's oral health status and behaviors is feasible, (c) the use of a dental assistant to collect data is reliable and valid, and (d) the use of dental assistants to collect oral health data is cost effective.

1) the use of clinical dental hygienists and dental therapists as examiners in a caries prevalence study is feasible, and 2) the use of a single examiner to examine all participants in a caries study is feasible.
